p.i: rit unum statutum legis. En Refch Lekisch existi-mavit omnia præcepta necessaria esse ad sanationem anima & perfectionis acquisitionem, atq; idèo ait

hoc est, gehennam dilatare os suum contra eum, qui omisit vel unum præceptum legis; Rabbi vero Jochanan judicavit, per liberam præstationem unius præcepti vel statuti, prout decet, sanari animam perfecta curatione.

main_text.head: IX.
main_text.p: Commendant cum Decalogi præceptis, tum Leges Ceremoniales, appellatas, tum Leges Forenses, Judicialesve, nominatas, negantes omnes has, picturas, typosque fuisse Messiæ, has figurasse ipsius mortem, beneficiaque, inficiantes Messiam Legis fuisse finem, ex Isaco Orobio, in Collatione cum Limborchio, pag. 115. In ultima quæstione petebam, ut assignaretur textus in Veteri Testamento, in quo Deus prædixerit, quod tota divina Lex, præter moralia, fuerat umbra, typus, & figura eorum, quæ tempori Messiæ futura erant; Inficiantes Leges has fuisse convictiones, argumentaque infignia infirmitatum, mortis, condemnationis, intermi-nantia maledictionem, sed Leges has caussas esse justitiæ, remissionis, vitæque æternæ, latas in eum finem, ut per earum observantiam mercedem acquirerent æternam, coramque Deo justificarentur, ex Rabbi Josepho Albo,

page.notes: The page is a 16th-century Latin text with Hebrew words (rendered in the transcription as Latin transliteration where the Hebrew letters could not be reliably reproduced); the Hebrew term "בני" and the Hebrew title "ןנב" beside "Ceremoniales" and "Forenses" were not reliably read. Marked text: "Refch" and "Lekisch" are doubtful. The Hebrew words "Lekisch" and "ɔ'pn" and "ɔ'ɔwn" could not be read with certainty and should be checked against the scan.
